Implement open-core model with Apache 2.0 (community) + BSL 1.1 (enterprise) licensing, compile-time feature gating in Core and Query Service, dual Docker image builds, and public community image publishing.

## Epic Quality Gates (run on completion)
- [ ] `make ci` passes (quality-rust, quality-go, quality-elixir-full)
- [ ] Community build compiles: `cd apps/core && cargo build --features community,analytics`
- [ ] Enterprise build compiles: `cd apps/core && cargo build --features enterprise,analytics`
- [ ] Community Docker image builds: `docker build --target runtime-community -t allsource-core:community apps/core`
- [ ] Enterprise Docker image builds: `docker build --target runtime-enterprise -t allsource-core:enterprise apps/core`
payload.title: Open-Core Licensing and Feature Gating

payload.description:
As a maintainer, I want proper license files (Apache 2.0 + BSL 1.1) and per-file headers on enterprise modules so that the licensing boundary is legally clear.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Replace root LICENSE (MIT) with Apache License 2.0 full text
- [ ] Create LICENSE-BSL file with BSL 1.1 text (change date: 2029-03-01, conversion license: Apache 2.0, use grant: AllSource Chronos community edition)
- [ ] Add BSL 1.1 header comment to enterprise files in apps/core/src/infrastructure/replication/ (mod.rs, protocol.rs, wal_shipper.rs, wal_receiver.rs)
- [ ] Add BSL 1.1 header comment to apps/core/src/infrastructure/security/rate_limit.rs
- [ ] Add BSL 1.1 header comment to apps/core/src/domain/repositories/tenant_repository.rs
- [ ] Verify: all non-BSL-marked files are covered by root Apache 2.0 LICENSE

Mark each item [x] as you complete it. Only close when all are checked.
payload.title: US-001: License Files and Headers

payload.description:
As a developer, I want community and enterprise Cargo features in apps/core so that enterprise code (replication, multi-tenant) is excluded from community builds at compile time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add Cargo features to apps/core/Cargo.toml: `community = []`, `enterprise = ["community", "replication", "multi-tenant"]`, `replication = []`, `multi-tenant = []`
- [ ] Update default features to include `community`: `default = ["server", "community"]`
- [ ] Gate replication module with `#[cfg(feature = "replication")]` in infrastructure/replication/mod.rs
- [ ] Gate replication startup block in main.rs with `#[cfg(feature = "replication")]`
- [ ] Gate tenant repository imports and usage with `#[cfg(feature = "multi-tenant")]`
- [ ] Gate multi-tenant auth code (tenant-related handlers/middleware) with `#[cfg(feature = "multi-tenant")]`
- [ ] Verify: `cargo build --features community,analytics` compiles without enterprise code
- [ ] Verify: `cargo build --features enterprise,analytics` compiles with all code
- [ ] Verify: `cargo test --features community` passes
- [ ] Verify: `cargo test --features enterprise` passes

Mark each item [x] as you complete it. Only close when all are checked.
payload.title: US-002: Cargo Feature Gating in Core

payload.description:
As an operator, I want an ALLSOURCE_EDITION env var in Query Service so that enterprise features (tenant management, quota enforcement, billing) are disabled in community mode.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add `:edition` config in config/runtime.exs reading `ALLSOURCE_EDITION` env var (default: "community")
- [ ] Create an Edition module (e.g., QueryServiceEx.Edition) with `enterprise?/0` helper
- [ ] Gate TenantContext plug on enterprise edition (community skips tenant resolution)
- [ ] Gate QuotaEnforcement plug on enterprise edition (community has no quotas)
- [ ] Gate billing-related routes (LemonSqueezy/Stripe webhook endpoints) on enterprise edition
- [ ] Verify: `ALLSOURCE_EDITION=community mix test` passes (community mode with dev-mode auth)
- [ ] Verify: `ALLSOURCE_EDITION=enterprise mix test` passes (full tenant/quota/billing pipeline)

Mark each item [x] as you complete it. Only close when all are checked.
payload.title: US-003: Query Service Edition Config

payload.description:
As a release engineer, I want Dockerfiles that produce separate community and enterprise images so that we publish distinct artifacts for each edition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Core Dockerfile: add `builder-community` stage with `--features community,analytics`
- [ ] Core Dockerfile: add `builder-enterprise` stage with `--features enterprise,analytics`
- [ ] Core Dockerfile: add `runtime-community` target (copies binary from builder-community)
- [ ] Core Dockerfile: add `runtime-enterprise` target (copies binary from builder-enterprise)
- [ ] Core Dockerfile: keep existing `runtime` target as alias for `runtime-enterprise` (backwards compat)
- [ ] Query Service Dockerfile: add `ARG ALLSOURCE_EDITION=community` build arg
- [ ] Query Service Dockerfile: pass edition as env var in runtime stage
- [ ] Verify: `docker build --target runtime-community -t allsource-core:community apps/core` builds on arm64
- [ ] Verify: `docker build --target runtime-enterprise -t allsource-core:enterprise apps/core` builds on arm64
- [ ] Verify: `docker build --build-arg ALLSOURCE_EDITION=community -t allsource-query:community apps/query-service` builds

Mark each item [x] as you complete it. Only close when all are checked.
payload.title: US-004: Dual Docker Image Builds

payload.description:
As a maintainer, I want CI to build and test both editions so that neither edition regresses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Update quality-rust Makefile target to run tests for both editions: `cargo test --features community` and `cargo test --features enterprise`
- [ ] Update .github/workflows CI to build both Docker image variants (community + enterprise)
- [ ] Add CI step for Query Service: run tests with `ALLSOURCE_EDITION=community` and `ALLSOURCE_EDITION=enterprise`
- [ ] Verify: `make ci` still passes with the dual-edition test matrix
- [ ] Verify: existing quality gates (quality-rust, quality-go, quality-elixir-full) still pass

Mark each item [x] as you complete it. Only close when all are checked.
payload.title: US-005: CI Pipeline for Dual Builds

payload.description:
As an open-source user, I want to pull community Docker images without authentication so that I can self-host Chronos easily.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Update docker-publish.yml workflow to push community images as public: `ghcr.io/all-source-os/chronos-core:<version>` and `ghcr.io/all-source-os/chronos-query-service:<version>`
- [ ] Update docker-publish.yml to push enterprise images with `-enterprise` suffix (remain private)
- [ ] Create docker-compose.community.yml at repo root with Core + Query Service (community edition), ready for `docker compose -f docker-compose.community.yml up`
- [ ] Verify: docker-compose.community.yml starts both services and health checks pass
- [ ] Document GHCR package visibility settings needed (manual step — note in PR description)

Mark each item [x] as you complete it. Only close when all are checked.
